summary: Head is a one-person SNAP household that receives Social Security disability benefits, so Head counts as a disabled member. Monthly gross income is about $2,146, under Michigan's 200% FPL categorical-eligibility limit of $2,610, and Michigan has no FAP asset test at or below 200% FPL. On every reading of the medical deduction, the computed allotment ($298 − 30% of net income) is negative. Federal law and Michigan BEM 213 still give one- and two-person categorically eligible groups the minimum benefit, which is $24/month for FY2026, so 12 × $24 = $288. The engine follows exactly this path; its net income of $1,755 differs slightly from stage 1's $1,747, which does not change the result. The $0 consensus overlooks the minimum-benefit rule.
